'''''Calystegia macrostegia''''', with the common names '''island false bindweed''' and '''island morning glory''', is a species of [[morning glory]] in the family [[Convolvulaceae]].

==Distribution==
The plant is native to [[California coastal sage and chaparral ecoregion|California coastal sage and chaparral]] habitats, along the coasts in [[Southern California]] and into [[Baja California]], Mexico.

It is found on all the [[Channel Islands of California|Channel Islands]], source of its common names.  It is also commonly found in the [[Peninsular Ranges]], [[Transverse Ranges]], and Outer Southern [[California Coast Ranges]].

==Description==
''Calystegia macrostegia'' is a woody perennial herb or small shrub which may be a low herbaceous vine or a stout, woody, climbing plant which can approach {{convert|9|m|ft}} in length. The triangular leaves may be over 10 centimeters wide.

The vine produces white, to very pale pink, to lavender blooms, often according to drought or temperature. The corollas are {{convert|2|-|6|cm|in}} or more in width.

==Cultivation==
''Calystegia macrostegia'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]], used as a [[vine]] and [[groundcover]] in [[List of California native plants|native plant]], [[xeriscape|drought tolerant]], and [[wildlife garden]]s.<ref>[https://www.laspilitas.com/nature-of-california/plants/1141--calystegia-macrostegia Las Pilitas Horticulture Database: ''Calystegia macrostegia'' (Island Morning Glory)]</ref> It is a pollinator plant for native bee species.
